ModMetaData.name: Shift Change
ModMetaData.author: MrBeverage
ModMetaData.description:
REQUIRES ODYSSEY (for the outfit stand) AND HARMONY.
Colonists change into the right clothes for the room they are going to, whether they are there to work or to enjoy themselves, and back out again afterwards.
Put a vanilla outfit stand in a room and put an outfit on it. Each stand dresses for one of two things.
Work. A colonist taking on automatic work of that room's kind (doctoring in the hospital, researching in the lab, cooking in the kitchen) changes into the stand's outfit before starting, and back when their work takes them elsewhere.
Recreation. The same machinery, for a colonist arriving to enjoy themselves. A frame of billiards, a hand of poker, an hour at the harp. A robe for the sauna, black tie for the games room.
Their own clothes wait in the stand either way, and come back exactly as they were, force-worn markers included.
Rooms are read from their role, so hospitals, laboratories, kitchens, workshops, barns and rec rooms all work with no setup at all.
Four optional controls per stand: - Shared (set owners) restricts a stand to the colonists you list: one for a personal kit, several to serve a group and nobody outside it. Left unassigned it is shared, like a bed, so a kitchen needs one stand per cook working at once, not one per cook. All / Men / Women tabs and an Assign all button make a stand the women's stand in two clicks, which matters for gendered clothing: a stand serves anyone who can wear something on it, so a shared stand holding a prestige robe and a ladies hat will put a man in the robe and leave the hat. - The stand's switch, labelled with what it currently dresses for, opens the checklist for rooms the game reads oddly, rooms that do two jobs, or a decorative stand you do not want used at all. It also names what the game reads the room as, which explains the surprises: a crib turns a hospital into a barracks. Recreation and work types are mutually exclusive (one outfit serves one purpose), so a room that does both wants two stands. - Change the whole outfit, off by default, is the difference between a lab coat worn over ordinary clothes and a sauna robe worn instead of them. Ticked, the colonist wears only what the stand holds, and loses whatever their own clothes were providing, warmth included. That is worth a thought before a robe rack in a cold biome. - Keep contents out of trade, on by default. Traders will otherwise buy anything sitting on an outfit stand: the uniform, and the owner's own clothes parked there while they are on shift. That is vanilla behaviour, it reaches caravans at the gate and ships in orbit alike, and nothing else about the stand prevents it. Untick it for a stand you keep as a shop shelf.
The stand's Allow removing items toggle is held off while the stand is in service, because turning it on exposes the contents to every colonist's outfit optimizer, which may wear the uniform as everyday clothes. It has never covered trade, which is why that is a separate switch. To take a garment back, use the eject button in the stand's Contents tab. To retire a stand and let haulers empty it, set it to Not used for shift changes, which frees the toggle.
Deliberately narrow, so it never fights you: - Automatic only, for work and recreation alike. A direct order is never delayed by a wardrobe trip, and a colonist already in uniform keeps it on. - Emergencies are never delayed, and nothing happens while the map is under threat. - Personal kit stays personal. A stand with owners serves only them, and nobody takes clothes out of a stand somebody else is using. - Passing through a room changes nothing; only doing the room's work does. - A meal break gets them out of uniform first, unless the food is already in their hands or their pack. - If a stand frees up while someone is already working in its room out of uniform, they step over and change, unless they are mid-treatment on a patient. - A Change back button appears on any colonist currently in a uniform, for when you want them out of it now.
Four things recreation will not do: drinking and drug-taking do not count, because fetching a beer is the same job in a bar or a corridor; reading is left alone, because a colonist picks their reading spot after setting off; outdoors is excluded for now, since every outdoor cell belongs to one enormous room, though a walled but roofless yard is its own room and still counts; and nobody is pulled out of bed, because vanilla gives patients recreation they can take lying down.
One setting: Unassigned stands are shared, on by default.
Adds no clothing, no buildings and no art of its own; it uses the vanilla outfit stand and whatever apparel you put on it.
Worth knowing before you build one: vanilla has no scrubs, no lab coat and no chef's whites, so there is very little to actually dress anyone in. Any apparel mod fixes that.
